reference: Numerics @ 2a0357a. Exact oracle values dumped from the REAL C# DifferentialEvolution/SobolSequence/Stratify (via tools/oracle_emitter, Task 9) and reproduced by tools/verify_oracles.py. Unlike every other toolbox/optimizer fixture (whose job is pinning ACCURACY against an upstream MSTest literal, so their tolerances are the loose Assert.AreEqual delta the C# test itself uses -- e.g. fixtures/toolbox/optimizers.json's de_booth case asserts abs tol 1e-4), this file's job is the CROSS-LANGUAGE guarantee: the same construct drives the C++, R, Python and C# harnesses, so a digest that reproduces in all four proves a seeded stochastic optimizer run AND two deterministic sequence generators are bit-identical across the packages -- the property both packages promise their users, mirroring the short_exact digest precedent of fixtures/estimation/fit_cross_language.json. The DE run reuses optimizers.json's de_booth construct (Booth objective, seed 12345) but pins the RAW converged value/parameters at digest precision instead of the rounded textbook optimum (1.0, 3.0) at MSTest's loose delta -- DE is stochastic and iteration-limited, so its converged point carries real trailing digits worth reproducing exactly. The Sobol and Stratify blocks reuse fixtures/toolbox/sampling.json's own cases (dimension 2, first 10 points; lower=100/upper=200/bins=100 linear stratification) at two of its already-pinned indices: both are closed-form/deterministic (no PRNG stream), so their cross-language risk is a code-path/arithmetic-order bug rather than a stream-divergence one, and reproducing them here alongside the DE digest is what makes this one fixture a single end-to-end proof of the whole cross-language toolbox surface (a stochastic optimizer plus two deterministic generators) rather than three separate ones.
